Lines 268–270 repeat the same construction pointwise for every `z ∈ sphere c r`.
findings.fix: Replace this hypothesis with independently obtainable geometric data that does not already contain the full target cluster set, or first prove from local connectedness/crosscut geometry that the displayed diameter bound holds; otherwise these criteria merely assume their substantive conclusion.
findings.issue: Both `subsingleton_clusterSetOn_ball_of_forall_exists_diam_biUnion_le` and the hypothesis used at line 268 are logically circular: `ζ ∈ closedBall ζ ρ`, so every displayed biUnion contains `clusterSetOn f (ball c r) ζ`; its bounded union having diameter ≤ ε for every ε already directly forces that cluster set to be a subsingleton.

summary: The two advertised crosscut criteria move the desired boundary uniqueness into their hypotheses, because the union being made arbitrarily small already contains the entire target cluster set.
